title: Delta SVD-EQ: Post-Hoc Spectral Equalization for LoRA Continual Learning

raw.stage1:
### Purpose
The contribution's purpose is to reduce catastrophic forgetting in sequential LoRA continual learning without any training-time modification. Several prior papers address catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, but none specifically focus on LoRA continual learning without training-time modification. Papers [1], [5], [6], [16], and [17] discuss catastrophic forgetting in continual learning broadly, but they do not explicitly target the combination of LoRA continual learning and training-free methods. Paper [16] introduces gradient-free continual learning, which is training-free, but it does not specifically address LoRA continual learning. Therefore, no prior paper fully matches the purpose.

### Mechanism
The mechanism involves Delta SVD-EQ: computing the task-specific LoRA delta, performing SVD decomposition, and equalizing the singular value spectrum while preserving the Frobenius norm. Paper [7] ("Spectral Surgery") discusses post-hoc refinement of LoRA using singular value reweighting, which is conceptually similar to modifying the singular value spectrum of LoRA updates. While the specific operation (root-mean-square replacement) differs, the underlying primitive of singular value manipulation for LoRA refinement is substantively equivalent. Papers [9], [12], [14], and [21] discuss SVD and its applications broadly, but they do not address LoRA or continual learning. Paper [29] introduces weight conditioning to narrow singular value gaps, which is related but not specific to LoRA. Thus, the mechanism is covered by [7].

### Evaluation
The evaluation claims the method satisfies four properties simultaneously: training-free, memory-free, post-hoc, and norm-preserving. Paper [7] evaluates a training-free, post-hoc LoRA refinement method, which overlaps with the evaluation design here. While [7] does not explicitly claim memory-free or norm-preserving properties, the evaluation design (post-hoc refinement of LoRA without training) is substantively equivalent. Papers [5], [16], and [20] discuss memory-free continual learning methods, but their evaluation designs differ significantly. No prior paper introduces a genuinely new evaluation design beyond standard continual learning benchmarks and metrics. Therefore, the evaluation is covered by [7].

### Domain
The domain is LLM continual learning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (LoRA). Papers [1], [4], [7], and [11] all work within the same general application area of LoRA continual learning or parameter-efficient fine-tuning for LLMs. While this contribution targets a specific sub-problem (training-free LoRA continual learning), the domain itself is not novel. Thus, the domain is covered by [1], [4], [7], and [11].
